date_note: LaLiga disclosed the attack in a press release dated 23 November; the release says the unauthorised access took place between 14 and 16 November.
title: LaLiga says cyberattack on a fan-services platform took personal data of registered users
geo_basis: headquarters of LaLiga (Madrid); the release gives no location for the platform
summary: LaLiga said on 23 November that a cybercriminal accessed one of its fan-services platforms between 14 and 16 November and extracted personal data of registered users; it says the attack was contained on 16 November and reported to the AEPD and police. Infobae reports Leganés called the data identifying and contact information; Real Zaragoza said it includes no credentials or banking information.
plain: LaLiga says a cybercriminal got into one of its fan-services platforms from 14 to 16 November and took personal data of registered users of LaLiga and some clubs. Clubs cited by Infobae warn of possible phishing.
exec: LaLiga says registered users' personal data was taken from one fan-services platform; it reported the incident to the AEPD and the police.
action: Clubs cited by Infobae advise verifying links, avoiding unknown attachments and contacting INCIBE for guidance, given possible phishing by email, text or phone.

evidence.quote: LALIGA sufrió entre el 14 y el 16 de noviembre un ciberataque

validation.note: Primary source: LaLiga's own press release (laliga.com, 23 Nov), read. Marca, AS and Mundo Deportivo also reported it but refused automated readers and were not read. The release names no clubs, gives no number of users and does not list the data fields taken; LaLiga says it is still analysing the scope. Infobae (23 Nov) read: relays clubs Leganés and Real Zaragoza statements on data types and phishing advice.

review.note: Compared title, dates 14-16 Nov, containment 16 Nov, AEPD and Policia Nacional report, scope and published date 23 Nov against LaLiga's own press release; evidence quote found; no advice given so action is fine
